headline: Highest risk is medium: Prefect can egress broadly while RisingWave is local-only, creating default data-flow and compliance exposure; no direct prompt-injection or write-conflict pathway is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, clipboard, MCP, or filesystem bridge is documented for Prefect and RisingWave. Prefect exposes network egress, but RisingWave shows no input surface that would ingest Prefect output as instructions. The pairwise prompt-injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, MCP server, or filesystem bridge is added between the agents, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate hosts or containers.
Do not bridge them with a shared clipboard or message queue.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect has broad network egress and touches workflow metadata, so it can transmit data off-host by default. RisingWave shows no egress and no data classes touched, so the main leakage path is one-way from Prefect rather than mutual. Because the pair lacks a documented isolation boundary, sensitive workflow metadata could leave the local environment.
conditions: IF workflow metadata includes secrets or regulated identifiers, Prefect can exfiltrate them over network egress.
IF both agents are placed in the same shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict Prefect egress with an allowlist.
Keep sensitive workflow metadata out of Prefect inputs.
Run RisingWave and Prefect in separate containers.
Review outbound destinations before enabling the pair.
requires-engineering: add DLP or redaction on Prefect outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Prefect has broad network egress, while RisingWave has no documented write or network surfaces here. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources, shared filesystem writes, or shared OAuth scopes. A capability conflict is therefore not evidenced beyond general orchestration overlap.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or database, conflict risk becomes material.
mitigations: Avoid giving both agents write access to the same path.
Use separate service accounts.
Serialize any shared writes through one orchestrator.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect can emit workflow metadata, but RisingWave has no documented input path showing it treats Prefect output as authoritative. Without a verified downstream action-taking loop, cascading error is possible only if an operator wires Prefect outputs into RisingWave automation. The current profiles do not show that default linkage.
conditions: IF RisingWave is configured to consume Prefect-generated outputs without validation, cascading errors become plausible.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Prefect and RisingWave.
Require schema checks on all handoffs.
Log and review transformed outputs before execution.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad egress, while RisingWave shows no data classes touched and no egress. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operator-chosen data placement. The other agent is not cited for a specific violation because no conflicting compliance surface is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Prefect to external services, compliance obligations may be triggered.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Prefect workflows.
Confirm retention settings before use.
Restrict outbound destinations.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
